title: Confidential Computing on Cohere Model Vault | Cohere
gist: Cohere announced the public beta of Confidential Computing on Model Vault, its dedicated managed inference service, running on NVIDIA H100 GPUs with Confidential Computing on Microsoft Azure. It protects data in use across CPU and GPU, encrypts request payloads end-to-end to an attested environment, and has the client refuse to send data unless remote attestation passes, aimed at financial, legal, public-sector and source-code workloads that had been kept off managed AI.

insights.claim: Cohere has launched the public beta of Confidential Computing on Model Vault, its dedicated, fully managed inference service, powered by NVIDIA H100 GPUs with NVIDIA Confidential Computing on Microsoft Azure confidential infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Confidential managed inference is now a commercial product, not a research concept, putting pressure on rival enterprise LLM vendors to offer equivalents.

insights.claim: Microsoft's Azure Confidential Computing product head Vikas Bhatia and NVIDIA enterprise software VP John Fanelli both endorsed Cohere Model Vault as a demonstration of managed AI with independently verifiable hardware-backed controls.
insights.speaker: Vikas Bhatia
insights.so_what: Co-marketing by both Microsoft and NVIDIA signals the Azure confidential-GPU stack is being pushed as the template for regulated AI workloads.
insights.quote: Enterprises need confidence that their most sensitive AI workloads are protected by more than contractual promises.
insights.locator: Built with Microsoft Azure and NVIDIA

themes.theme: Protecting data in use and in transit

insights.claim: Cohere Model Vault's confidential computing targets the third state of data, data in use, by running inference in a hardware-isolated environment spanning CPU and GPU that keeps workload memory away from privileged infrastructure software and operators, with GPU memory protected and CPU-GPU traffic encrypted.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Data-in-use protection widens the addressable market for hosted LLMs into data previously barred from the cloud.

insights.claim: Model Vault encrypts application payloads end-to-end to the attested confidential environment instead of relying only on connection-level encryption, so requests and responses cross intermediary infrastructure without exposing plaintext, while customers keep the same Model Vault API and request formats.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: No application rewrite is needed, which lowers switching friction for enterprises trying confidential inference.
insights.locator: End-to-end protection for sensitive request contents

insights.claim: In Cohere Model Vault, customer-side software checks signed attestation evidence about the processing environment's hardware, firmware and software against an approved policy before sending data, and refuses to send the request if the policy is not met, moving the trust model from "trust us" to "verify it yourself".
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Cryptographic verification replacing contractual trust could become a procurement requirement in regulated sectors.
insights.quote: This changes the trust model from "trust us" to "verify it yourself."

insights.claim: Cohere CTO Phil Blunsom says hardware attestation lets Model Vault customers verify that their data is protected from unauthorized access, including from Cohere itself.
insights.speaker: Phil Blunsom
insights.so_what: Positioning the vendor as unable to see customer data is Cohere's pitch against hyperscaler-native and frontier-lab LLM offerings.
insights.quote: they also can verify that their data is protected from unauthorized access, even from Cohere.
insights.locator: Enterprises should not have to choose

insights.claim: Cohere argues the enterprise AI bottleneck has shifted from whether AI can do a task to whether the required data can safely be used with AI, and targets confidential Model Vault at financial fraud investigations, legal privileged-document search and due diligence, public-sector data, patents and research, engineering design documents, and proprietary source code.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: If correct, data-governance tooling, not model capability, gates the next wave of enterprise AI spend in regulated verticals.
insights.quote: the question is no longer whether AI can perform a task. The question is whether the data required for that task can safely be used with AI at all.
insights.locator: Unlocking AI for sensitive enterprise workloads

insights.claim: Cohere acknowledges that confidential computing on Model Vault does not eliminate all risk and does not replace application security, compliance, contractual controls or data-residency requirements.
insights.speaker: Cohere
insights.so_what: Residency and compliance demands remain separate buying criteria, so sovereign deployments are still needed.
insights.locator: Confidential computing does not eliminate all
